concept.name: Displayed liquidity
concept.definition: Trading interest that is visible to the public before execution - quotations and displayed orders included in consolidated quotation data. The SEC's equity market structure concept release classifies registered exchanges and ECNs as displayed trading centers, which executed about 74.6% of NMS share volume in late 2009.
concept.intuition: It is the liquidity everyone can see quoted before deciding to trade.
concept.mechanics: Exchange members and market makers communicate their best-priced bids and offers to their SROs under Rule 602, which disseminate them to vendors; displayed orders generally receive execution priority over undisplayed interest at the same price, and maker-taker pricing rewards posting displayed orders.
concept.failure_modes: Displayed size has shrunk with algorithmic and high-frequency quoting, and flickering quotes mean a share of displayed liquidity is practically inaccessible; relying on it alone misjudges true market capacity.
concept.misconceptions: Displayed liquidity is not the whole market: dark pools, internalizers, reserve size, and iceberg orders add a large undisplayed component.
concept.example: A 500-share bid displayed at the NBB is displayed liquidity; the same order's 5,000-share reserve balance is not.

citations.source: SEC, Concept Release on Equity Market Structure, Release No. 34-61358, 75 FR 3594
citations.section: Part III.A Trading Centers (displayed vs undisplayed trading centers)
